keyFindings.text: **Decision capture.** `AGENTS.md:147-151` delegates save composition and "what the writer touches" to `save-workflow.md`. That file now specifies the whole behaviour: a `--full-auto` save writes each `operatorDecisions` entry into the packet's `decision-record.md` while a plan-only save writes nothing [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/references/memory/save-workflow.md:261], the five runtime sweeps are named [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/references/memory/save-workflow.md:262], and the writer matches an existing hand-written record before appending [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/references/memory/save-workflow.md:277]. The delegation sentence stays true; no `AGENTS.md` edit.
sources: `git diff --name-status v4.0.0.16..v4.0.1.0`; `git log --oneline v4.0.0.16..v4.0.1.0 -- AGENTS.md "REPO RULES.md"`

keyFindings.text: **Doc rewrite guard.** The guard exists at `.skilled/skills/sk-doc/shared/scripts/doc-rewrite-guard.py` and the release makes it a pre-commit step for form-only rewrites [SOURCE: .skilled/changelog/skilled/v4.0.1.0.md:196]. It is **not** in the primary pre-commit gate — that hook runs comment hygiene, agent-mirror sync, mirror parity, prompt-card sync, MCP mutation-class, compiled-routing re-mint and spec derived-metadata re-mint [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/git/README.md:18] — so a rule could be argued for. It is reached instead through routing: `sk-doc`'s router carries a `RENDER_LEDGER` intent weighted 4 on keywords `doc rewrite guard`, `doc-rewrite-guard.py`, `kept every claim` [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/ROUTER.md:174], and `AGENTS.md:70` already sends every first `.md` write through `sk-doc`. Adding a second statement to `AGENTS.md` would create the duplication `AGENTS.md:247` explicitly avoids ("Go to the owner rather than a summary here").

keyFindings.text: **`skill-hub-routing.md:61` placement sentence vs `package_skill.py --strict`.** The *placement half* is now machine-enforced: a skill that keeps its router inside `SKILL.md` fails strict packaging [SOURCE: .skilled/changelog/skilled/v4.0.1.0.md:60], and the checker's own routing-shape rules RS-002/RS-003 state the same invariant [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-skill/scripts/package_skill.py:1420]. The *reachability half* of the section — the two-stage replay — has no check. Keeping the rule costs one sentence and covers the half no tool covers; deleting it would leave the replay undocumented. Keep.

keyFindings.text: **`skill-hub-routing.md` vs `12a-router-contract` / `12b-routing-shape`.** Not redundant. The new checks assert shape and presence (a file exists, a link resolves, a section moved) and the ratchet only lets recorded debt shrink [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/parent-skill-check.cjs:2233]. The rule's subject is reachability, which the checks explicitly do not test and cannot: a hub passes every one of them with a mode no request can reach. The rule's opening claim is the one thing a green run still cannot say.

keyFindings.text: **Nothing is stale.** All three codes still exist in the checker (23 occurrences of `RS-002|RS-004|RS-005` in `.skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/parent-skill-check.cjs`), so the rule is not pointing at a retired name.

**The rule's own contract forbids it.** `REPO RULES.md` §4 states that `skill-hub-routing.md` "carries no route-selection guidance: the mechanics stay in the skills, and the rule points at them" `[SOURCE: REPO RULES.md:98-101]`, and the rule does point: it sends the reader to section 7 of `parent-skills-nested-packets.md` `[SOURCE: .skilled/repo-rules/skill-hub-routing.md:71]` and says "The commands are in the reference above" `[SOURCE: .skilled/repo-rules/skill-hub-routing.md:89]`. Putting `RS-002`, `RS-004` and `RS-005` into the rule is precisely the mechanics-in-the-rule duplication the carve-out was written to prevent.

**The sentence is more true than when it was written.** `:78` says the per-hub gate "asserts only presence, never reachability" `[SOURCE: .skilled/repo-rules/skill-hub-routing.md:78]`. Checks `12a` and `12b` assert shape — a sibling file exists, a relative pointer exists, no router section remains in `SKILL.md`. Shape is not reachability, so the rule's distinction is exactly the right frame for the gates that appeared. Adding the codes would narrow a general statement into an inventory.

`f-iter003-001`'s sentence "That phrase is the sole acknowledgment the check accepts, and it is read from the block only" is **false on both halves**: no phrase is accepted, and nothing is read from the block.
f-iter004-001 (P2) — `f-iter003-001`'s central mechanism is wrong: the `delivery prefix` guard reads the canary's stdout, never the repository block, and nothing silences A6
f-iter004-002 (P2) — The proposed `:70` wording does fit: 89 bytes, 13 bytes of headroom, and every repository skill has a sibling `ROUTER.md`
f-iter004-003 (P3) — `f-iter002-001` is gate detail the rule rightly delegates; no rule edit, and the residual gap belongs to an `sk-doc` reference outside this packet's surface
f-iter004-004 (P3) — No `REPO RULES.md` trigger-table row should route to a v4.0.1.0 doctor command; all four already fire existing rows

The design warning built on it — that a rule teaching the escape by quoting the words into the block "permanently silences A6" — is **false**. Writing `delivery prefix` into the repository block has no effect on A6 whatsoever. The warning must be dropped, not softened; keeping it would ship a rule that names a footgun that does not exist.

What survives from `f-iter003-001` is the narrower, still-true part: the 16,384-byte delivery prefix is real, it is enforced twice (manifest pins plus canary), it is stated in no rule file, and the live run reports 16,368 of 16,384 `[SOURCE: AGENTS.md:70]`-adjacent headroom from row A6.

ruledOutDirections.text: **"`system-spec-kit` SKILL.md §3" may have lost its content to the router move.** It did not; §3 keeps "Retrieval and Continuity", "Reranking" and the declared-loss sentence.

**`advisor_recommend` looked removed.** `.skilled/agents/code.md` and `.skilled/skills/README.txt` both show the verb `l`, which reads as a rename. The frozen contract settles it the other way: nine commands, each accepting snake, kebab and camel spellings, `advisor_recommend` first in the table [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/references/runtime/cli-front-door-contract.md:47], and the built CLI contains seven occurrences. `AGENTS.md:67` is correct and `l` is a separate short id.

**`sk-create-goal`'s `references/budget-and-handoff.md` may have moved under `sk-doc`.** It sits at `.skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-goal/references/budget-and-handoff.md`; `AGENTS.md:155` cites it by skill name, not by path, so the extra folder does not stale the citation.
**A doc-rewrite-guard rule is missing from `AGENTS.md`.** Rejected: `sk-doc`'s router owns the intent and Gate 2 already routes there.

**Sweeping the rule files for v4.0.1.0 impact as a first move.** Only two of thirteen files changed in the range — `communication-handoff.md` (4 lines) and `skill-hub-routing.md` (8 lines) — and both changes were themselves router-related. The rules layer is ahead of `AGENTS.md`; a rule sweep on this axis yields nothing until the rules' own internal citations are the target.

**Treating `.skilled/changelog/skilled/v4.0.1.0.md:27`'s spec-folder list as the change inventory.** It names nine packets and "smaller packets for the fixes"; the git range covers 458 commits and 33,921 paths, so the list is a pointer, not an inventory. The named-packet approach cannot substitute for the tree probe.

**`## MACHINE ROUTER` in `skill-hub-routing.md:61` is stale because real headings are numbered (`## 3. MACHINE ROUTER`).** Not stale. `package_skill.py` extracts heading titles and compares `title == 'MACHINE ROUTER'`, so the number prefix is stripped before comparison [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-skill/scripts/package_skill.py:1174], and its diagnostics print the unnumbered form the rule uses [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-skill/scripts/package_skill.py:1420]. The rule quotes the heading title, which is the stable identifier.

**`parent-skills-nested-packets.md` §1-2 did not actually carry the `routingClass` table or the `ROUTER.md` locations.** It does: table at line 132, stage-two file table at 42-55, canonical sentence at 79.

**`skill-hub-routing.md` became redundant when the routing shape became gated.** It did not, for the reason in f-iter002-003: shape is not reachability, and the rule's whole point is that distinction.

**Probing relative links with `realpath` on macOS.** It does not exist there, so the probe silently reports every link as broken. Use `os.path.exists(os.path.normpath(os.path.join(dirname, target)))` from Python instead. Recorded so a later iteration does not spend a call rediscovering it.

**The rule's §7-covers-the-surface-list citation was off by one section.** It is not; §7 is "ADDING A MODE TO AN EXISTING HUB" and holds the 11-row table [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-skill/references/parent-skill/parent-skills-nested-packets.md:245].

**`/doctor:install` and `/doctor:symlink` need a rule because they mutate a project.** No: the commands own their own plan-then-yes discipline, `blast-radius.md` governs any install, and `AGENTS.md:289` already delegates the inventory.
**`AGENTS.md:70`'s proposal is simply wrong.** No: it is substantively right and self-consistent with Gate 5 and the advisor. Only the `one line` parenthetical and the byte budget need correcting.
**A rule is needed about which lines an update may overwrite.** No: A7/A8 plus the note line own it; the gap is capacity, not ownership.

**A rule is needed for conversation playbook scenarios.** No: `sk-doc`'s `playbook-conversation` intent already routes the request, and the runner is documented by the skill that ships it [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/ROUTER.md:103].
**The `§4`-before-`§3` order was introduced by the manifest.** No: identical order at `v4.0.0.16`.
**The worker-session nudge removal leaves a dangling rule.** No: zero references to a nudge in the rule layer; only an unrelated English use of the word.

**Treating "the manifest requires a rule about which lines an update may overwrite" as a single question.** It splits into ownership (settled by A7/A8) and capacity (unstated, and load-bearing). Asking it as one question would have produced either a duplicated rule or a missed budget.
**`skill-hub-routing.md:78` should name `RS-002` / `RS-004` / `RS-005`.** Rejected: mechanics in the rule, against `REPO RULES.md:98-101`.

**A `delivery prefix` line in the repository block silences A6.** False. `own` is canary stdout screened for `MISSING:` / `BLOCKED:` `[SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/agents-md-check.cjs:461-463]`; document prose cannot enter it.

**A trigger-table row should route to `/doctor:agents-md` or `/doctor:install`.** Rejected: `REPO RULES.md:5-6` and `:18` make the table a rule-file router; the commands already fire rows 42, 44 and 45.

**Measuring only the variants already on the table.** Iteration 3 tested the two wordings it had and concluded about "any version". A budget question has to be answered by measuring the cheapest candidate, not the two most discussed.
**No `ROUTER.md`-naming wording fits the budget.** False at the short end: the 89-byte form lands at 16,371, 13 bytes inside.

**The canary is silent past the prefix, so A6's fallback is the only signal.** False. The canary emits its own failure containing `delivery prefix` `[SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-review/scripts/check-rule-copies.js:428]`, printed as `MISSING:` `[SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-review/scripts/check-rule-copies.js:440]`.

**Treating iteration 3's A6 read as sufficient because it quoted the right file and line.** The citation was correct and the inference from it was inverted — the code was read as parsing the document when it parses a subprocess's stdout. For any row that shells out, the variable's provenance (`output` at `:450`) has to be established before its predicate is interpreted. Recorded because this is the second time in this packet that a correct citation carried a wrong inference.
